title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

providers.name: Snowflake
providers.scope_notes: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

controls.name: Authentication policy AUTHENTICATION_METHODS
controls.what: Allow-list of auth methods; omitting PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN, KEYPAIR, WORKLOAD_IDENTITY or OAUTH blocks that method for the account or user.
controls.setting: CREATE/ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY ... AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER SET AUTHENTICATION POLICY
controls.quote: PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN: Allows users to authenticate with a programmatic access token.

controls.name: PAT_POLICY MAX_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS / DEFAULT_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS
controls.what: Sets the default (15 days) and maximum (365 days) PAT lifetime; lowering the max breaks longer existing tokens.
controls.quote: Specifies the maximum number of days that can be set for the expiration time for a programmatic access token.

controls.name: PAT network policy requirement (NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION)
controls.what: By default a user must be subject to a network policy to create or use PATs; admins can relax this.
controls.quote: the user must be subject to a network policy with one or more network rules to generate or use programmatic access tokens

controls.name: PAT role restriction requirement
controls.what: Service-user PATs must name a single role by default; admins can also require it for person users.
controls.quote: you must specify the role that will be used during sessions authenticated with that token.

controls.name: MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege
controls.what: Only roles with OWNERSHIP or this privilege on a user can manage that user's PATs, key pairs or workload identities.
controls.setting: GRANT MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS ON USER ... TO ROLE
controls.quote: you must use a role that has the OWNERSHIP or MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC AUTHENTICATION METHODS privilege on that user.

controls.name: Disable / revoke PAT
controls.what: Admins can disable or remove a PAT; disabling a user's login disables their PATs.
controls.setting: ALTER USER ... MODIFY / REMOVE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN
controls.quote: You cannot recover a programmatic access token after you revoke it.

controls.name: Network policies (account / user / security integration)
controls.what: Restrict inbound access by IP or private endpoint; integration-level policy overrides user and account policies.
controls.setting: CREATE NETWORK POLICY; ALTER ACCOUNT/USER/SECURITY INTEGRATION SET NETWORK_POLICY
controls.quote: the most specific network policy overrides more general network policies.

controls_unknown: Edition requirements for authentication policies are not stated on the reference pages.
Whether Snowflake OAuth (as opposed to External OAuth) can be disallowed via AUTHENTICATION_METHODS; the OAUTH value is documented as 'Allows External OAuth'.
No account-wide policy found to force named key pairs or cap key-pair lifetime; legacy RSA_PUBLIC_KEY keys never expire.
Docs differ on how to unblock privileged roles for custom OAuth clients (account parameter vs Snowflake Support).
Whether the WIF quote 'disable it' covers the DEFAULT identity (docs say DEFAULT must use SET/UNSET WORKLOAD_IDENTITY).

authentication.summary: Snowflake OAuth/External OAuth, key-pair JWT, programmatic access tokens (PATs), and workload identity federation.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Account/user network policies. By default PERSON and SERVICE users need a network policy to use a PAT; SERVICE_AGENT users do not. Authentication policy NETWORK_POLICY_EVALUATION can drop the requirement or skip enforcement.

renewal.summary: No refresh; rotate the PAT (new secret, extended expiry) or generate a new one. Lowering the policy maximum makes existing longer-lived PATs fail.

administration.summary: Authentication policies restrict auth methods/security integrations; RBAC and PAT role restriction, blocked roles, expiry/revocation.
administration.conditions: Avoid treating default PAT safeguards as immutable. Verify client/driver and cloud support for federation.

offboard.details: Disabling a user, which is what Okta SCIM deactivation does, automatically disables the user's PATs and aborts the user's running queries.

inventory.details: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.CREDENTIALS WHERE type = 'PAT' lists PATs for all users.

inventory.ui: Snowsight > Governance & security > Users & roles > (user) > Programmatic access tokens (per user)
inventory.cli: SQL: SELECT * FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.CREDENTIALS WHERE type = 'PAT'; per user: SHOW USER PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKENS FOR USER <name>

SQL: ALTER USER|ACCOUNT ... SET NETWORK_POLICY = ; PAT requirement: ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY

SQL: ALTER AUTHENTICATION POLICY

SET PAT_POLICY = (DEFAULT_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS = n MAX_EXPIRY_IN_DAYS = m); per-token expiry: EXPIRATION_DATE in ACCOUNT_USAGE.CREDENTIALS

usage.cli: SQL: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY WHERE first_authentication_factor_id = '<CREDENTIAL_ID from CREDENTIALS>'

reads.cli: SQL: SELECT ... FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.ACCESS_HISTORY ah JOIN QUERY_HISTORY qh USING (query_id) JOIN LOGIN_HISTORY lh ON qh.authn_event_id = lh.event_id WHERE lh.first_authentication_factor_id = '<pat_credential_id>' (or join SESSIONS on login_event_id)

token_format.notes: Format not published. GitHub detects it as secret type snowflake_programmatic_access_token (partner + push protection) but does not publish the regex. Sent as Authorization: Bearer; SQL API token type PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY
log_sources.notes: Successful and failed logins, 365 days, up to 2h latency. INFORMATION_SCHEMA LOGIN_HISTORY table functions cover 7 days. PAT logins have FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR = PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.SESSIONS
log_sources.notes: One row per session, 1 year, up to 3h latency; links to login via LOGIN_EVENT_ID. Does not track SQL API transient sessions.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.QUERY_HISTORY
log_sources.notes: Queries per SESSION_ID with AUTHN_EVENT_ID, 365 days, up to 45 min latency.

log_sources.name: SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.CREDENTIALS
log_sources.notes: Current credential inventory (PAT, KEYPAIR, WIF types) with LAST_USED_ON; up to 2h latency; deleted credentials are not included. PAT rows have TYPE 'PAT'; ADDITIONAL_DETAILS has ROLE_RESTRICTION, ROTATED_TO.

log_sources.name: GitHub secret scanning partner program
log_sources.notes: Leaked PATs in public GitHub repos are reported to Snowflake, which auto-disables them.

credential_id_fields.notes: Credential ID of the PAT used; join to CREDENTIALS.CREDENTIAL_ID.
Name of the PAT for a given secret (with USER_NAME, STATE).

lifecycle_events.event: ALTER USER … ADD PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN
lifecycle_events.notes: SQL command; find in QUERY_HISTORY.QUERY_TEXT. Default expiry 15 days, max 365.
FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR value in LOGIN_HISTORY (success and failure).

lifecycle_events.event: ALTER USER … ROTATE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN
lifecycle_events.notes: New secret, same name; old secret expires per EXPIRE_ROTATED_TOKEN_AFTER_HOURS.

lifecycle_events.event: ALTER USER … MODIFY PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN
ALTER USER … REMOVE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN

anomaly_cues: PAT login from a CLIENT_IP never seen for that FIRST_AUTHENTICATION_FACTOR_ID
PAT created by a CREATED_BY user different from the token owner, especially on a service user
PAT created with long expiry (near 365 days) or with network policy bypass (ADDITIONAL_DETAILS.MINS_TO_BYPASS_NETWORK_POLICY_REQUIREMENT)
Burst of failed PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN logins against many users
PAT use right after creation from an IP unlike the creator's session
CREDENTIALS STATUS = DISABLED from GitHub auto-disable: review earlier use of that token

containment.steps: Identify owner of a found secret with SELECT SYSTEM$DECODE_PAT('<secret>'); run ALTER USER <u> REMOVE PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN <name> (or MODIFY … SET DISABLED = TRUE to preserve for review). For wider compromise, ALTER USER <u> SET DISABLED = TRUE, which aborts running queries and disables the user's PATs.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether sessions opened with a PAT end on removal. ALTER USER SET DISABLED = TRUE aborts running queries. Removed PATs drop out of CREDENTIALS, so snapshot the row before removing.

sample_query.query: SELECT login.event_timestamp, login.user_name, login.client_ip, cred.name, cred.created_by FROM SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.LOGIN_HISTORY login JOIN SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.CREDENTIALS cred ON login.first_authentication_factor_id = cred.credential_id WHERE login.first_authentication_factor = 'PROGRAMMATIC_ACCESS_TOKEN' AND login.event_timestamp > DATEADD(day,-30,CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) ORDER BY login.event_timestamp DESC;
sample_query.purpose: List PAT logins with token name, creator and source IP for the last 30 days.
